facts.fact: The World Bank study states that the Directorate of Nationality, Passport and Immigration under the Ministry of Interior has been tasked with establishing a civil registration system; the study gives no date for this, so its publication date (August 2018, on research carried out in 2017) is used.

systems.owner: Directorate of Nationality, Passport and Immigration, Ministry of Interior

systems.platform: card with thumbprint image, 2D barcode and ICAO-compliant machine-readable zone; 14-digit alphanumeric personal identification number
systems.owner: Directorate of Nationality, Passport and Immigration, Ministry of Interior
systems.tiers: 170 registration devices across the country and embassies and about 100 handheld read-and-verify devices, largely at the borders; over 1 million cards issued

systems.owner: Directorate of Nationality, Passport and Immigration, Ministry of Interior
systems.tiers: issued since 2015 to citizens of all ages

note: The South Sudan section is about the national ID and Nationality Certificate (identity class). It also says a birth certificate is not required for a national ID in South Sudan and gives birth registration at 14.7 per cent (SHHS-2, 2010) in one table and 35 per cent of under-fives (UNICEF) in a country box: shares of births, not of offices. The civil-class entry is a system yet to be established, with no description of how it would make a record.
